description:
## What

Move the `handle_error` case/handler block into its own file.

## Source to move (from `src/fetcher/crest_http_client.cr`)

- `handle_error(ex : Exception, url : String)`
- `handle_uri_error(ex, url)`
- `handle_socket_error(ex, url)`
- `handle_timeout_error(ex, url)`
- `handle_ssl_error(ex, url)`
- `handle_request_failed(ex, url)`
- `handle_unknown_error(ex, url)`

## Why

- Pure error-translation: turn one exception class into another with a uniform
  shape. No HTTP state, no DNS, no config reads beyond what is already on
  `RequestConfig`. Single responsibility.
- A standalone `ErrorMapper` is the right place to add new mappings (e.g.
  `IO::Error`, `Socket::ConnectError` subtypes) without touching the
  orchestration class.
- Currently the case/when chain is 20 lines with 6 handlers — non-trivial and
  duplicated state (the `url` is passed through unchanged to every handler).

## API target

    class Fetcher::CrestHttpClient::ErrorMapper
      def map(ex : Exception, url : String) : Nil
      # raises the appropriate Fetcher::* error
    end

Caller becomes:
    rescue ex
      record_failure(domain) unless domain.empty?
      ErrorMapper.new.map(ex, url)
    end

## Constraints

- Must raise the same exception types with the same messages as today
  (tests assert on `DNSError`, `TimeoutError`, `HTTPClientError`,
  `HTTPServerError`, `HTTPError`, `FetchError`).
- The `(catseye)` NOTE comments about including the URL move with the code.
- HTTPClientError is the special case that doesn't re-raise from
  `perform_request`'s `rescue ex : HTTPClientError` — keep that behavior.

## Done when

- New file exists; `crest_http_client.cr` calls `ErrorMapper.new.map(ex, url)`.
- `crest_http_client_error_handling_spec.cr` passes unchanged.
title: Extract ErrorMapper into src/fetcher/crest_http_client/error_mapper.cr
